title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

reading.body:
This is an insider misuse case, not a model failure. A person with legitimate access to a deployed system used it for a purpose it was not intended to serve. The Flock camera system was built to support police work, and the searches described were run against a private individual the officer had previously dated.

The failure sits at the access layer rather than the model layer. The system performed the searches it was asked to perform, and the harm came from who was asking and why. Catching this kind of misuse requires auditing who queries the system and against whom, and comparing those queries to case records, not improving the accuracy of the underlying tool.

What is not established is whether the allegations are true. A criminal complaint is an accusation, not a finding, and the internal affairs investigation and the Select Board hearing have not produced a public determination in the facts given.

reports.title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

summary:
A Stow police officer, Jason Rogers, is accused of misusing police databases to track a woman he previously dated. The woman said she ended the abusive relationship about five years ago and changed her identity, phone number, and social media habits. She discovered this summer that Rogers had searched for her location through the Flock camera system multiple times in 2024 and 2025. The department said Rogers also used other state systems to obtain information about her.

Stow police filed a criminal complaint against Rogers on July 17 for possible state law violations. After a four-week internal affairs investigation, the department placed him on paid leave in July, then unpaid leave as of July 31. The woman has a restraining order against him for at least a year. The police chief said a Select Board hearing next week could decide Rogers' employment status.
